utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there were no preliminary matters. Therefore, the witness can be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Masal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind that you you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning. And thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, General Masal.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We are going to continue with where we left off yesterday and discuss activities that occurred between the 13th -- excuse me, the 11th and 13th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32181 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, before you is an ABiH Supreme Command report related to activities on the 11th of February, 1993, so this is the report of your opposing forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English and the bottom of page one in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the paragraph in this report related to OG Gorazde. This report indicates: "In OG Gorazde's zone of responsibility, there was artillery fire on almost all populated places as in the preceding days. We do not have information about killed and wounded but material damage is significant." This is what happened pursuant to your order: Populated areas of Gorazde were shelled on the 11th; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this report, we can see that this is the period in question. However, I'm not surprised by this. Their reports were daily reports and they were accompanied by significant propaganda in the sense of major destruction and major casualties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please answer the question. The question is whether that is what happened, that populated places were shelled those days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, one can see that from the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not whether we can see it from the report. The question is whether it happened. Whether you have any knowledge about it happening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the document that I was shown yesterday, we could see that there was an order to open artillery fire on certain targets in the Gorazde sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the question now is whether that shelling took place, as described in this report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not receive a report, i.e., I did not have feedback from the command of the 3rd Brigade that that shelling had actually materialised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is your answer you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether fire was opened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, there's discussion of threats to block humanitarian aid convoys and exposing Medjedja to fierce artillery fire unless the demands to release prisoners are met. Your brigades were ordered to fire at Medjedja after this; right? Just to be clear after -- after the 11th/12th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. My brigades were given an order to open fire, but I'm really not sure that I understand your question completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I'm directing your attention to the fact that this report indicates there have been some threats relating to humanitarian convoys in that if these demands were not met, that fire would be opened up on Medjedja. What I'm asking you is that after this time, your brigades were ordered to fire on Medjedja; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know where threats came from or who ordered whom to open fire on Medjedja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this document into evidence, 65 ter 32181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7229, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7229 is admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to go rather quickly through the next two reports with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32302 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a similar report to the one we just looked at but it's from the next day. It's an ABiH Supreme Command report related to activities on 12 February 1993. In the third paragraph, the report states: "In the zones of operations of the Visoko, Igman and Gorazde OG, the aggressor" -- in reference to your forces -- "opened sporadic artillery, tank, mortar, PAT and PAM fire at our positions." Your units did not fire at populated areas of Gorazde on Friday, 12th of February, 1992, is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7230, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7230 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32182 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an ABiH report related to the activities on Saturday, 13 February 1993. In the -- just confirming where it is. In the fourth paragraph, the report states: "In OG IB Gorazde's zone of responsibility, the aggressor shelled the town of Gorazde and other populated areas in the free territory from the direction of Cajnice and Rogatica." This report reflects that the 3rd Podrinje Brigade in Cajnice who you issued your order to did carry out its orders and fired a concentration of artillery at Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. As it is now mixing and matching what is contained in the order that was discussed yesterday and what is contained in this document. I believe in the order yesterday Mr. Weber focussed on the fire on the market-place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear, Mr. -- could you please -- it was a compound question anyhow. Could you please split it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll just make it really simple. This -- this information shows that your units fired again in populated areas of Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not ruling this out, but I was not aware of every activity of my subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7231 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get some clarification, sir. When you say you are not aware of what your subordinates did and you don't know whether they carried out your order, are you trying to tell this Chamber that you were playing marbles? You would just give an order and you don't care whether it was carried out? You don't follow up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, certainly not. I believe that we were serious and we would not have been playing marbles. Every order that was issued to a subordinated command had to be followed by a regular combat report on tasks accomplished. I told you that it was just possible that that's what had happened. I don't know whether the following day a regular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you have answered me. You say you were not playing. Now, in -- what you are telling me about reports is my next question. Now, of the system within your command and control was that subordinate orders -- subordinated units give a report to their superiors about the carrying-out of orders that they were given. Are you telling this Court that you never received such a report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is not what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... a report. If that's not what you are saying. Did you receive the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I received reports from subordinated commands every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what did the reports say about the activities -- the order that you gave for attack on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, to correct you. But it's 13 February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 13 February, I'm sorry. What report did you get about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to say a daily combat report of a unit -- I can't remember what was reported on that day. I can't remember that part of the report which concerns that particular task. It eludes me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which part of that report do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that report at all. The document that was shown to me by the Prosecutor here is something that covers an event 20 years ago, and I don't remember that combat report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, you have voluntarily come here to testify about events that happened 20 years ago, okay? So we're asking about those events, and you have told us here of things that you remember that happened 20 years ago. That's why you wrote a statement and we're still asking you about the same things, okay? Now, what part of that report do you remember? You say you don't remember this part. What part do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've answered. I don't remember the report that I received on that day. I don't remember a host --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're changing your answer. That's fine. Thank you very much. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to change topics. I don't know if you have any other questions related to the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your brigades were ordered to target schools and mosques also; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32183 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say the number again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an 8 March 1993 order from your deputy commander, Colonel Parezanin. It orders the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Podrinje Brigades to fire five to seven rounds at targets that are then specified. The areas listed in this order were all inhabited by non-Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Largely Muslims, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: One of the locations where the 2nd Podrinje Brigade is ordered to fire is the school in Medjedja. In fact, your unit -- your brigades were ordered to fire at schools; right? We see this in the order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was signed by my deputy. I wouldn't wish to comment upon this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, your command issued this order to fire at Medjedja after demands to release prisoners were not met. This is what happened; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this had to do anything with the request to set prisoners free. You are establishing that link, but I can't. I can't establish that link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, apart from establishing links, were orders given to shell or to give artillery support aiming at the school in Medjedja? If you remember, tell us; if you say, I don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to explain why you don't know. You don't know. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The 3rd Podrinje Brigade from Cajnice is ordered to fire at the mosque in Gorazde. This is the same brigade that you ordered to fire upon the market; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued an order to open fire on the market sector. I did not issue this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, sir. My question was: This was the same brigade for whom you issued the previous order; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same brigade. It hasn't changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7232, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Witness, a question that was not yet asked to you. Do you have any knowledge about this order to fire on the mosque in Gorazde? If so, please tell us what you know; if you don't know, please tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience, Your Honours, I was just checking something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on and discuss with you Operation Mac. Operation Mac 1 was carried out at the end of May and beginning of June 1993; right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P5173 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the 22 May 1993 VRS Main Staff order for Operation Mac from General Mladic. For the Chamber's reference, the code name of the operation is on the last page above the signature. We see that the order was sent to the Drina Corps and to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, SRK. Is this correct that Operation Mac was a joint operation between these two corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an operation of the Drina Corps with part of the forces, just part of the forces that were resubordinated to the Drina Corps and the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to item 2 where General Mladic states: "The task of the Army of RS is to carry out offensive operations and ocisti in Central Podrinje, disperse and destroy Muslim forces in the general area of Gorazde and enable the Muslim civilians to move away (relocate) to other areas (central part of the former BH) or to accept the" --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could have the next page of the translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "... or to accept the authority of Republika Srpska and thus create the conditions for the return of the Serbian population to the left and right banks of the Drina River." This task is a reflection of the VRS position on civilians; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the position towards the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, according to this order, this operation was to take place in two stages lasting eight to ten days with the first stage lasting five to six days. General Mladic ordered that the operation was to begin no later than 27 May 1993. This is when Operation Mac was executed by the Drina Corps and the SRK, between the 27th of May and approximately 5 June 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During this time, your brigades carried out the task assigned by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got the order from the command of the Drina Corps, and I myself issued tasks to the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the course of this operation, your brigades, again, shelled the town of Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan of activity of artillery of the brigades in this operation is something that I did not have an opportunity to see personally. I commanded and controlled part of the operation in my area of responsibility, so as for these details, whether the town of Gorazde was shelled, I cannot say anything to you about that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you really saying as a person with a significant amount of artillery experience and the commander in the zone of responsibility of Gorazde that you're not aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is speaking aloud, which he's not supposed to do. And also no nodding to witnesses or to anyone else, Mr. Mladic. Just focus on the case. Please proceed. Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honours, actually I'm just going to go to the document. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32235 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 31 May 1993 article from the Los Angeles Times entitled: "Pounding of Sarajevo most brutal in months; Balkans; shelling of capital seems to underscore ineffectiveness of west's latest BiH peace initiative." I'd like to direct your attention to the third paragraph of the article. The article reports: "One of the other proposed safe areas, the eastern city of Gorazde, has been pounded for three days by an even more intense artillery assault, and the Serbian attackers were reported to have broken through the beleaguered enclave's last line of defence? "Government-controlled Sarajevo Radio said the rebels overran Gorazde after inflicting heavy casualties in a salt that rained more than 1.000 shells on the town the previous day. Thousands were attempting to flee the city, the broadcast reported. It also said 11 soldiers had been killed and 34 wounded." This was how Operation Mac was carried out; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page, there's information provided by Commander Barry Frewer who is an UNPROFOR spokesperson he reported that UN Military Observers had tried to reach Gorazde three times to assess the situation but were turned back by Serbian gunmen. This information shows that your units were still continuing to deny entry into Gorazde from international organisations; right? That's what we see here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is certainly correct because during intensive combat operations in the zone of responsibility, such convoys were not allowed to move about in the area. Allow me just one sentence. Operation Mac on this date, units were 35 kilometres away from Gorazde. At the very end of the operation, we had just reached Ustiprace which is 12 kilometres away from Gorazde, and it was on that line that Operation Mac ended. You can see on the basis of this document and propaganda that the town of Gorazde had purportedly been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to Sarajevo, I just want to ask you about this before we move on, Commander Frewer said that during a 17-hour period that included the dawn battle, UN Military Observers in the capital counted 310 mortar and heavy artillery impacts, presumably of shells fired from Serbian positions, in the government-held city centre and three blasts in Serb-held areas. The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was shelling the city of Sarajevo during the course of Operation Mac. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Goes beyond --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Goes beyond the scope of the direct examination. Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But isn't it true that in cross-examination you can -- it's not limited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then he has to lay foundation, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. That's not what the rules require. Only if the witness gives answers which are not in line with the case of the Prosecution, then the Prosecution should put to the witness what their case is. That's the rule. Nothing else. Let's -- I have a question, but the witness has answered the question anyhow. So I take it, Mr. Ivetic, there's no problem there remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just before we move on to something or your question, I just wanted to put on the record that the basis of my questions related to Operation Mac is the fact that he comments on the order as part of his statement as an associated exhibits. So it's in that context I am also asking about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say that basis for the objection wasn't there, and I commented, rather, on the rule that apparently was invoked by Mr. Ivetic. And the witness said he didn't know. Now I have -- Witness, you said, and we're looking at this document only briefly now, so perhaps you could assist us. You said you can see from this document and propaganda that was -- that Gorazde was purportedly taken. Now, could you help me where exactly that is stated in this article? That Gorazde was taken, where you said that you went only to 12 kilometres of that town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, it was the gentleman, the Prosecutor, that read that out from this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That the town of Gorazde was taken? Was that read out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. That was read out, that Radio Sarajevo or Radio Gorazde, I'm sorry. The gentleman, the Prosecutor read that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do not know if the witness is getting it from the phrase --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Transcript, page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Transcript page 14, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Line 19. Is that what the witness said, isn't it? You can see on the basis of that document and propaganda that the town of Gorazde had purportedly taken. That was the last line of the witness, not of what Mr. Weber read.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Line 19, page 13. 19 and 20, page 13, Mr. Weber's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let me then see. Oh, that's rebels overrunning Gorazde, yes. Now I see. Yes, I may have misunderstood that the beginning, apparently it's interpreted by the witness and by you as well, Mr. Ivetic, that overran Gorazde is taking -- is equal to taking the city but let's leave it to that. Whereas the witness told us that they only moved from 35 kilometres of Gorazde to as close as 12 kilometres to the town of Gorazde. Whereas earlier yesterday the witness made a distinction between the town of Gorazde and the Gorazde area. Let's leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honours. I'm told that the B/C/S version of this document in the specific part actually says captured Gorazde as well, so I don't know if that's something that we should address to CLSS or what the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if we need to verify the translation into -- into B/C/S -- apart from what was read to the witness, I don't know whether it was translated in a similar, as you suggest, way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know either so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That can be verified. First, the translation can be verified. Second, the interpretation, if there's any need, can be verified as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I think there's an additional problem when we look at the original of this document which is B/C/S this is a translation from a Los Angeles Times article. This is a transcript of an article in the Los Angeles Times and that is -- if I understood that correctly, again translated into English in this document. Oh, what is the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... in e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was asking Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I -- okay. Let Mr. Weber answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The original is in English that we then requested a translation in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In e-court, it appears as M001-3077 is the original, which is in the English language indeed. Whereas, M001-3077-B/C/S is then the translation. Mr. Weber, will you take care that the translation will be verified, whether, in the B/C/S, it is translated that the town or Gorazde - I do not know yet - was captured. Meanwhile the document will be MFI'd. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P7233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we hear from you, Mr. Weber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 03422 for the witness. Page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 4 June 1993 UNPROFOR report from General Morillon regarding a meeting he had with Radovan Karadzic on 3rd of June. The first paragraph states: "There is evidence to indicate that Serb forces continue to press an attack against BiH positions around Gorazde. There has also been a consistent refusal by the Serb military leadership to allow UNMOs into the area." There are then references to three incidents that occurred on the 1st of June, 1993, including a shelling in Dobrinja, and the sniping of two French soldiers at the airport in Sarajevo. The second paragraph starts: "I drew Karadzic's attention to the fact that his actions in Gorazde had violated the sanctuary of an UN-declared safe area." Sir, you were aware that Gorazde was a declared safe area at the time of Operation Mac; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that it was declared a safe area, but the activities concerning the safe area were not completed fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P7234, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Maybe we can just address a brief matter before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I see you still have a copy of your statement in front of you. If there's any way you could please turn to paragraph 15 and I'll ask you some questions on it. In paragraph 15 of your statement, you state: "I have never personally observed any civilians accepting the invitation to remain in any liberated territory while respecting the laws of the RS." This is because the non-Serb civilians left as a consequence of VRS operations; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In another part of the same paragraph, you say: "There were some ethnically pure Muslim villages between Visegrad and Rogatica, such as Satorovici, Osovo, Okruglo and Burati." You then go on to indicate that the Muslim residents lived in these areas which were controlled by the VRS up until the Dayton Agreement was signed. Then you claimed they moved out of their own free will. I want to seek a clarification with you about the date that you referred here. That date is not accurate in terms of when they moved out. And, in fact, the Muslim villagers in these areas moved out by the second half of 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the residents of these villages moved out in that period of time. Part of them did, as far as I was informed. Now whether entire villages moved out, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's look at what you said in your previous testimony. Sir, I'm going to call up your Popovic testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32310, page 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before we further look at that -- Witness, you said you don't know whether they stayed there until the Dayton Agreement. But that's what we find in your statement, isn't it, where it reads, they were: "Until the Dayton Agreement was signed, they remained in this area which was then under the control of the VRS until the Dayton Agreement was signed, and then moved out of their own free will." And now you're telling us that you don't know whether they stayed there, remained until the Dayton Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received information that most of the inhabitants stayed on until the Dayton Agreement because in mid-1994 I left that area. I just received information that part of the population or, rather, the majority of the population of these four villages stayed on in these villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you should have done under those circumstances, to make a clear distinction between what you know on the basis of your personal observations, which apparently, from mid-1994, was not the case any further, and, second, that the information received was not that they remained but that most of them remained. So your statement to which you attested is inaccurate in that respect. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Masal, I'm actually going to read out your whole previous answer on this topic from the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could have the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In response to a question, you stated: "In my area from the very beginning of the war until nearly the end of the war there were four villages which were purely Muslim, according to their ethnicity, this was between Visegrad and Rogatica. They belonged to Rogatica municipality and these villages were" -- and if we could please have the next page. "Satorovici, Osovo, Okruglo and Burati. That population remained living on the territory controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska and under the Serbian civilian authorities. A large influence was exerted on them to remain by a retired general of the former JNA, Asim Hodzic, who was advanced in years; but when combat began in Bosnia-Herzegovina, he was living in the village of Satorovici. As he was in poor health, I had occasion to meet him personally when he was being transported from Rogatica via Visegrad and Uzice to Belgrade at the military medical academy. The population in these villages remained peaceful, and they lived there until the second half of 1994 peacefully. Then they moved away probably in the direction of Sarajevo or somewhere in Central Bosnia." Do you stand by your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. To be fair, if you're going to broach that topic you should read the entirety of the testimony on transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know what you're going to refer to. If it is a matter which can you raise in re-examination, then you should do so. If it really is unfair -- incomplete is not for parties necessarily under all circumstances, unfair. So please carefully look at what you want to add and see whether that can be appropriately done in re-examination rather than to intervene in the line of questioning of the cross-examination. I leave it to you, Mr. Ivetic, to carefully think about it and to see whether it can be done or whether it should not wait until re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I don't know if Mr. Weber is aware of transcript page 29155 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prosecution's questioning, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you please look at the source given by Mr. Ivetic and then you decide whether it's better to include it now or to leave it to Mr. Ivetic to raise it in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I can assist further, it's lines 1 through 10 so you don't have to read the whole page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, is it right that that was in re-examination in that case as well, so apparently it's a matter that can be raised in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, it was in cross-examination by the Prosecution, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that it is something that Mr. Ivetic would be free to lead. The main fact I'm going after is just his previous statement that he said that they had left in the second half of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are aware that Mr. Ivetic will -- is in a position perhaps to draw the attention of the witness to other parts of his testimony in that case. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you stand by your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer that question whether what was just read to you as your previous testimony, whether you stand by that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was an oversight on my part, that instead of 1995, I said 1994 in my previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that -- was that an error or was it ... I mean, it's not entirely clear to me. Do you say you made a mistake in the testimony that was read to you, or did you make a mistake today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mistake was made in my previous testimony. I suppose that I meant the end of 1995 and it seems it turned out that it was -- the end of 1994. Because the end of 1995 is the end of the war. In the introduction to this answer in my previous testimony, I said at the end of the war, and then when I mentioned the year I stated that it was in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we're at the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the break. Witness, would you please follow the usher. We would like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Masal, you are familiar with the Strpci abduction which occurred on 27 February 1993 where a group of armed persons took Muslim passengers off a train and these passengers were never seen again. You're familiar with this event; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Belgrade-Bar railway line ran through your zone of responsibility at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for some 12 kilometres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This railway line also runs through Sandzak, a border region between Serbia and Montenegro; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Sandzak is not a border region between Serbia and Montenegro. It is a part of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The railway line runs through Sandzak; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along its border. Only along its border.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Strpci train station, which is where the abduction occurred, was located in the municipality of Rudo; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There was a plan to be abduct passengers from the train prior to the 27th of February; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The abduction was carried out pursuant to your orders; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32202 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm actually going to go through a number of materials related to this event today. This is a -- this is the first one. It is a 1 February 1993 letter from the director of defence preparations for the public railway transport company in Belgrade to the general director of the company. The first paragraph states: "A few days ago, more precisely on 28 January 1993, I was informed by the head of the Uzice STP section, Zivanic that members in of the Serbian army in Rudo municipality will stop a train and abduct its passengers. The entire operation is to take place on the section of the Belgrade-Bar railway line running through Bosnia and Herzegovina, most likely at the Strpci junction or the Goles railway station." So in fact there was plan to be abduct passengers either from Strpci or Goles prior to 27 February. That's the case right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no plan in place. At least as far as my command is concerned and my brigade commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next section of the letter, it indicates that the collegium of the railway line, the police, and the State Security Service of the Serbian MUP and the assistant defence minister of Serbia were contacted. Did any of these people bring up any concerns with you or your superior commands about a plan to be abduct passengers from the train?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody brought it up with me. I don't know if any of my higher-ranking officers had any conversations with the officials you have just -- that just mentioned. At least they never informed me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7235 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32204 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 21 February 1993 TG Visegrad order to the 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 5th Podrinje Brigades. You issued this order; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The order starts: "Pursuant to a request from the Supreme Commander of the Army of Republika Srpska ..." That's referring to a request from Radovan Karadzic which you received through your chain of command; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under number 4, you ordered: "Immediately inform us of any captured Muslims, who are from the territory of Sandzak, and should you not have any, organize and carry out an action with the objective of capturing them." You ordered your units to capture Muslims from Sandzak if they did not have any; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did order, but I did not order them to capture civilians but, rather, Muslims who often travelled from Sandzak through my zone of responsibility in the direction of Gorazde and Sarajevo. This has nothing to do with civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7236, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P6652 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 22 February 1993 report from the 2nd Podrinje Brigade Command, one of the brigades that you sent the order to the day before. This report is sent to your command and states: "There are no paramilitary formations or groups in our brigade combat activity zone. It should be noticed that there are groups under the brigade command that use the names that could remind you of the paramilitary groups Osvetnik, Garavi, Skakavci, and similar. "All these groups are respecting our brigade command, carrying out its tasks and make the part of the intervention company." You were aware of the information in this report; right? It's to your command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In fact, you reported this information to the Drina Corps Command; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The commander of the group known as the Garavi was Boban Indjic; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Is a question that needs to be specified which of the groups, as I understand this document there are two groups that have that name. Which group is Mr. Weber's question directed at? Without -- without -- without -- I can't go any further with the witness present to endanger --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why couldn't the witness answer the question and you further specify if there's any chance of any confusion, then you could repair that during re-examination. Isn't it? Let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The document talks of two groups and mentioned just one group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, Mr. Weber referred to one of the groups directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours are misunderstanding my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- Witness, do you understand English, the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not a word? Apart from yes or no perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones, please. Mr. Ivetic, the question put by Mr. Weber was whether the commander of the group known as Garavi was Boban Indjic. And I see that in the document reference is made to the groups that used the names that could remind you of paramilitary groups, among them Garavi.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of the paramilitary groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of the paramilitary groups. You missed the "the," which implies that there's a group in the army with that name, and a paramilitary group with that same name, which group is the question directed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... whether the one implies the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the English it does, Your Honour. That's the plain meaning of the English text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me read. Is that your understanding of the English text? My understanding of the English text is, and I give it to you so that you can comment on it. That it should be noticed that there are groups under the brigade command that use the names that could remind us of the paramilitary groups and then they are listed, paramilitary groups by the name Osvetnik, Garavi, Skakavci and similar. So it's not a limited list. I do understand this to mean that within the brigade command groups are active which remind of paramilitary groups of the same name. It doesn't give any -- doesn't give any clue as to whether those paramilitary groups do still exist or do not exist or whether it's the same group that now is within the brigade command still using the name it used earlier. That's all open, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is open and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore now Mr. Weber asks the witness whether the commander of the group known as Garavi - and that could be one or more groups and that's still open - whether that was Boban Indjic. Now, first of all, if the witness is aware of more than one group, then he will tell us. Then he will -- may not understand the question. And if he answers the question, you could still further explore that, whether he was referring to the group within the brigade command or whether he was referring to the paramilitary group that you could think of that had existed. That can also be further explored, but there's no need at this moment in view of the questions, which are still open, to hint at the possibility that both groups, the one within the brigade command and the one the names reminds us of, whether they were still in existence. That can be further explored. The witness can answer the question. Can you please put on your earphones again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was put to you - and I'll re-read the question to you - I'll read the ... whether the commander of the group known as the Garavi was Boban Indjic. Can you tell us whether that was the name of the commander of the group known as the Garavi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I know that Boban Indjic was the commander of the intervention company. This is the first time I hear that he was the commander of a group that called itself this way. From the moment I joined the tactical group until the end of my stay with the tactical group, Boban Indjic was the commander of the intervention company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Milan Lukic was the commander of the group that was called the Osvetnik; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the previous question, Witness, you told us that you were familiar with the name of the person. Milan Lukic, are you familiar with his name as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the war, I had only two occasions to meet with Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so you're familiar with the person by that name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the abduction of the passengers from Strpci, there were eight Muslim individuals that were taken from the train that were from the Sandzak region. That's what happened; right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32205 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarification before you go to this next document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, at page 29, line 3, you asked the witness whether -- I beg pardon, page 28, line 5. You said, "In fact, you reported this information to the Drina Corps Command; right?" And the witness answered yes, and you were talking about this document which has these paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could revisit that after going through this next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If you revisit it, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 28 February 1993 - so a day after the abduction - Drina Corps security and intelligence report from Jovo Maric to the VRS Main Staff. The report relates to the Strpci abduction which is discussed in the first two paragraphs and, as you see, there's reference in the second paragraph to Boban Indjic, leader of the Garavi Sokak armed group. In the third paragraph, if we could scroll down, and maybe if we could actually enlarge it a little bit for the witness, if it's possible, the report states: "The Garavi Sokak group operated, along with other similar ones, as a paramilitary; however, according to the latest report from Colonel Dragisa Masal, commander of the TG Visegrad, the said Masal claims that these groups are in the formation of the 2nd plpbr intervention company and ... they respect and carry out the orders of their command. In addition to the cited persons, Milan Lukic was also involved in the abduction, who is known from before as an extremist." This is the information that you reported to the Drina Corps Command; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, Witness. The question was whether you reported to the Drina Corps Command as is described in this document, which there's no suggestion that this is your report. Could you please answer the question that was put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't. My command did not send a report to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, it's not whether you sent a report but whether you reported. There are various ways of reporting something. Was what was in this document recorded as what was reported by you to the corps command, did you ever report, in whatever way, that information to the Drina Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In an oral conversation with the commander of the Drina Corps, I informed the commander, Zivanovic, about the event in so much as I knew based on the information received from the command of the 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question again is what was -- did you, in that conversation, or at any other point in time that these groups are in the formation of the 2nd plpbr intervention company and whether they respect and carry out the orders of their command. Was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that within the intervention company there were groups under those names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you also tell them that they were carrying out orders of their command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your previous answers were pretty evasive, in view of what you're telling us now: I did not send a report. That wasn't asked. You, in a conversation, gave this information to the corps command, if I understand you well. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 32205 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7237, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Masal, I'm going to change topics again and go onto another matter. During your time as the commander of TG Visegrad, you kept imprisoned civilians in your zone of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time when I took this position, there were no civilians in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 09716 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 7 October 1993 TG Visegrad report from you to the Drina Corps Command. This document relates a -- relates to a request of the UK command intelligence organ. Is it that the UK refers to the Uzice Corps of the Yugoslav, or VJ, army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Uzice Corps and the Drina Corps co-ordinated with respect to matters of security and intelligence; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The first part of the report indicates that the UK Command is requesting delivery of an imprisoned civilian who was being held in Rudo at the time. In item 2, you state: "The said imprisoned civilian was captured during a raid in Herceg Novi where, according to the UK OB's allegation, he had been staying since the start of the war (fled from Gorazde)." In item 3, you go on to state: "He was brought to the prison in Rudo from the prison in Foca in order to be exchanged for our citizens who have not left Gorazde." What you told us a moment ago is not true. The fact is you kept imprisoned civilians in your zone of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this case, and with full responsibility, I can assert that this is the first time I hear of this. Who signed that report instead of me, I cannot say right now, but I state with full responsibility that I was not aware of this case at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How were civilians were being brought to the Foca prison from Herceg Novi?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The prison in Foca was the KP Dom that you're referring to; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just heard that. I never checked that. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So you just heard that. You heard that from your subordinate commands; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Foca is not in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You heard that from your superior commands; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody had any need to tell me that the prison in Foca is the KP Dom. I heard that existed before the war, the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What prison in Rudo are you referring to in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Misstates the testimony of this witness. He said that he had not signed this document so to call it "what you are referring to" is a misstatement of the evidence on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the report that's under your name it refers to a prison in Rudo. What prison is this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade did not have a prison. That can only be a prison within the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7238, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7238 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Weber, if you would allow me, I would like to go briefly back to the Garavi group and put an additional question to the witness. Witness, you told us that you, in a conversation, you had informed the -- that groups under the names that were mentioned were within your brigade and that they were carrying out orders of their command. Now, one of these groups was the Garavi. Who was at the head of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know. Since these are lower levels of command, this is probably a soldier. I could not have known all the soldiers within the tactical group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But apparently you were aware of the existence of those groups which are known by those names. But you had no idea that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew on the basis of the information that I received from the intelligence organ of the 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And they told you the names of the groups but not who were in those groups.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just for clarification, we were shown that document before. I don't know the number recorded, but we did have that before us. I think it was P6652.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm ... So you were familiar with the existence of a group under that name in the intervention company but you had no idea who was leading that group, if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the area of Visegrad, the 2nd Podrinje Brigade secured the Uzamnice prison facility; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32208 for the witness. Actually, excuse me, strike that. I think actually the last answer will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that prisoners were beaten at Uzamnice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in Visegrad, I heard that Milan Lukic had mistreated detained persons, but I personally never established that and I was never able to establish that. I just had information that there had been mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Who did you receive this information from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subordinate commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You received it from Luka Dragicevic, commander of the 2nd Podrinje Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You're acknowledging he's the commander. That's the person you received the information from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand. I admit that Luka Dragicevic was the commander of the brigade, yes. I think that at one moment I heard that you mentioned Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Actually, sir, I just asked you if prisoners were beaten at Uzamnice. You then offered Milan Lukic as a name of a person who had mistreated detained persons and you said: I just had that information that they had been mistreated. I asked you simply who did you receive this information from, and you said: The subordinate commander. The subordinate commander who told you this information was Luka Dragicevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one moment, it seemed to me that you said Lukic Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just answer the last question, whether the subordinate commander who told you this information, whether that was Luka Dragicevic, I think if you could answer that question, we can then move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32207 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're still with the same subject, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 2 April 1993 TG Visegrad list of imprisoned persons who are located in the 2nd Podrinje Brigade's prison. This is a list that you sent to the Drina Corps Command; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The 2nd Podrinje Brigade's prison that -- that you're referring to is the Uzamnice prison; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see at the top of the page that this is being sent to Lieutenant-Colonel Cerovic. Could you tell us his position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps, as far as I know, he was in the Department for Morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who directed you to prepare this list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty now who it was. Probably it went through the organ for morale from the Drina Corps to the 2nd Brigade, and then the 2nd Brigade provided that to me, or to my command, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You recognise the names on this list to be names of Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see at points 3 and 4 that the people referred to here were born before 1920. TG Visegrad detained people over the age of 70; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot accept that because from when I took up my post, not a single person was detained. Obviously these are persons who were detained in 1992 at this facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Just so we're clear on where you're getting that information for [sic], you're referring to the individuals, let's use numbers 3 and 4 as an example, and the information that they had been detained since their date of capture on 10 October 1992. That's what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously all of this has to do with 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 of the English translation, at point 19, that's a 10-year-old Muslim girl who'd been detained since 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Point 20, that's an 8-year-old Muslim girl; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 32207 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7239, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Could we, nevertheless, seek some information. You said this was about -- was about 1992. Now, the document dates from April 1993, and it says: List of imprisoned persons who are located at the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade prison. It doesn't say who were located but who are located. Do you have any explanation as to why such a list was sent under your name, saying that they are located where you are denying that there was anyone in detention? Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have an explanation because I still maintain with full responsibility that from my arrival there and throughout the period of my command, I did not see a single civilian in Uzamnice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But we now see a document with your name under it, which lists persons up to very elderly persons, very young persons, as being detained in the 2nd Light Infantry Brigade prison. Now, I do understand that you say it's not true, but, of course, that -- I'm seeking a real explanation rather than a repetition of what you said before. How it is possible that such a list is provided, if you say there were no persons detained, no civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously -- well, I don't know whether -- whether you will accept this explanation of mine, but this is a document that was sent not through the chain of command but, rather, through a particular service. That is to say, the information service or rather the morale service. Who wrote this in my command? Since I had two operations officers who were in the command, in addition to the Chief of Staff, now who wrote this, and on the basis of which period, I cannot say to you right now with a great deal of precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I heard your answer. Now this document also refers to the prison within this brigade. Was there any prison within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I've referred to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I think that -- isn't it true that the witness said something about that there was only MUP prisons and no --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh that was in Rudo. Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Rudo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have one short follow-up question. You said: "I did not see a single civilian in Uzamnice." Did you hear about a civilian in that prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. I heard before I arrived there, before I assumed command in Visegrad, before I assumed my duties there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And did you hear about detained civilians in that prison after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have one question which is a bit referring to an earlier part of your testimony. You said you heard about Mr. Lukic, who had mistreated prisoners. Did you investigate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because Lukic was not within my units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was not subordinate to you in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Masal, in response to Judge Fluegge's question just now, you said that you had heard before you arrived, before you assumed command in Visegrad, that -- about civilians at Uzamnice. Who did you hear this from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from civilians. If you want me to be specific, my wife's friend from school at the time when I was not at home, spoke to my wife before all communications were cut with Bosnia-Herzegovina, and she mentioned that a relative of hers was at that facility. And beforehand, that had been a warehouse of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if we reconciled whether or not the document was admitted. I know I tendered it. Ms. Stewart helps me. Thank you. Sorry. Your Honour, I see that we're also at time for a break. I'm going onto a new topic. If we could take the break a minute or two early, just not to split the next topic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You were going to revisit a matter that I was trying to raise a little earlier. Are you still going to revisit it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Forgive me if I'm off, but are you referring to whether or not he reported the information about those groups to the Drina Corps? I -- forgive me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I seem to think you addressed it with the document that you said you would like to have a look at first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think you did address it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, Your Honours. I don't know if it's a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's a good time for a break. But I'd first like to deliver a decision in private session. So if first the witness could be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we return into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We take a break, and we resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you tell us whether you're on track in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have been informed that I'm at two hours and 20 minutes and I am on track and on time in terms of our four-hour estimate. And Your Honours, it does look -- and we did speak briefly with counsel about this, the next witness who I know may be present, it does look like we probably will not get to that witness today. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think it would be wisest to excuse the witness for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, there was one issue remaining that was, you remember the publication in an English newspaper, what was the original what was the translation. Now we do see that the original is in English but, of course, it's not directly taken from that newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a transcript of that newspaper. Could you try to find out whether it's a literal transcript of what is published in that newspaper or whether there's anything which does not for the full 100 per cent correspond with the published article.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours. And I do understand that you're referring to the Los Angeles Times relating to the Mac -- to the course of examination I was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was what I was referring. We dealt only with one newspaper article today. We'll continue. Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Tactical Group Visegrad participated in Operation Zvijezda 94; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32225 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 3 May 1994 TG Visegrad operation analysis regarding Operation Zvijezda 94.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could just flip to the last page quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This analysis is from you; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please return to the first page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, your analysis indicates that the Herzegovina Corps commander had an idea to launch an operation to liberate the territory of the Serb municipality of Gorazde. The liberation of Gorazde was the objective of Operation Zvijezda 94; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Serb municipality of Gorazde had not been established prior to this operation; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Legally under that name, no. However, Gorazde municipality was both Serb and Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 4 of the B/C/S original and page 5 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the end of this analysis, you state as your conclusion: "The units of TG Visegrad managed to fully achieve the objectives set in the Zvijezda 94 operation. 135 square kilometres of territory was liberated. All conditions were created for the establishment of the Serbian Municipality of Gorazde, the return of the residents to the territory and the further activities on the full liberation of the city of Gorazde." This was your conclusion; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The area that was taken during this operation included villages near the town of Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You refer to the return of residents to their territory. Is it correct that you were referring to Serb residents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 32225 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7240, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7240 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32220 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say the number again, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 26 March 1994 TG Visegrad order for further operations pursuant to Operation Zvijezda 94. The order is from you to your subordinate brigades and copied to the Herzegovina Corps for their information. Is it correct that this operation began at the end of March 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to section 2, the task that is in this section and it's underneath the locations of the villages, you communicate, it states: "Break up and destroy enemy forces in the zone and create conditions for the liberation of Gorazde." This was the specific task that you conveyed to your units; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
