utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of both versions, and I'm focussing on section 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under section 6 regarding fire support, you state: "The chief of artillery of the TG shall determine firing positions and plan fire for the duration of the operation and the required quantity of ammunition as approved by the Main Staff VRS." General Mladic was the person from the Main Staff who approved the fire support during this operation; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Then who was the person that -- that authorised it, that approved it, from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fire support for the units in the operation was from own forces and own tools. And as for the necessary quantities of ammunition for the operation, were to be requested from the main command all the way up to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm asking you a fact: Who from the Main Staff approved this during the course of the operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ammunition for the operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the phrase actually reads: "The artillery chief shall determine firing positions and plan fire for the duration of the operation and the required quantity of ammunition as approved by the Main Staff VRS." Who from the Main Staff was approving this during the operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is unclear in this context --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- one question. The ... was the planned fire for the duration of the operation, was that approved by the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fire support was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just seeking clear answer. Was the required quantity of ammunition approved by the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who, in the Main Staff of the VRS, approved the quantity of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to approving ammunition for particular operations, it was the deputy commander of the Main Staff who did that. His decisions were implemented by the logistics sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was that the case in this year as well; and who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose so, since I received the necessary quantities of ammunition through the Drina Corps. I sent my request along the command line, and I suppose that the command of the Drina Corps forwarded my request to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You suppose all that. In the document, we read that it was approved by the Main Staff of the VRS. Who was, then, the deputy commander who would have approved this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence, 65 ter 32220.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7241 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During this operation, the VRS destroyed villages around the town of Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32230 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 5 April 1994 UNMO Gorazde sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the second page of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It reports on what is going on in the area of Gorazde, and I'd like to focus your attention, starting with the phrase where the UNMOs communicate: "Villages burned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not clear we have the correct page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it was the bottom of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that mean number ten would not exist because we see on the English screen that it is immediately before paragraph 11 whereas we have paragraph 9 on the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we have the next page of the B/C/S. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's no number ten in the English original either, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's the case, then if it would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: A part missing I mean, a part that's cut off, so I don't know whether that says number 10. That's my problem with this document there's some lines missing at the bottom of the first page in the English and at the top of the second page in English but I don't see a number 10 anywhere in the English original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I am just focussing on particular information here. I see what the top of page 2 looks like. If I could just go to the preceding page in the B/C/S again, and I believe, actually, the part I want to focus on is at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if there would be -- and let's just have a look. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see there's possibly some translations issues here. If I can read out the part I would like to use in the English original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would do that, it may well be that the English version is not complete so at least you should try to find a complete English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to draw your attention to a part of this report. It states: "Villages burned, destroyed by BSA are Kordici, Ljeskovik, Radmilovici, Nevorici, Stanici."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Here B/C/S ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Then it goes on: "Ogleceva (school and mosque), Ljeskovic, Dragoli, Bosanje as reported by local authorities and refugees. These villages have on average between 25-30 families." These were areas located outside the town of Gorazde; correct? The villages I have just mentioned to you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with any of the names of these places. I think or, rather, I'm sure that they are not in my zone of responsibility. None of them are. The villages of Kopaci, Obarak and Ustiprace were in my zone of responsibility, as well as the foot of Kozara and Kozara or, rather, those villages. And they were not destroyed which is corroborated by the fact that the Serbian population returned into those settlements and that's where the Serbian Municipality of Gorazde was established. Bear in mind that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we're talking about the villages. The village of Ogleceva where the school and the mosque were located, this is actually, in fact, an area just to the south of Gorazde of the town, right by Dragoli, and Bosanje - correct? - is in that area too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in the direction of Foca. Not my zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, you said you don't know anything about these villages but then you say they were never destroyed because the Serbian population returned into those houses. Did I hear -- am I interpreting you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be MFI'd to resolve the translation matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can also have the MFI defined if we can find a better copy because the section that's being cited is particularly where there's the illegible portion which this text is a continuation of, so to have a meaning of what it means, we need to have the complete document, not this incomplete version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean at the top of page 2 where we only can see and in Gorazde city whereas it's difficult to read the first lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Line or lines we do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, and I think it's also possible at the bottom of page one might be part of this as well. I don't know. Because, again, there's no number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So Mr. Weber it will be marked for identification. You're invited to find a complete version in the English and then, of course, have a -- a -- a corresponding version in translation in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, I will look to see if we have one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will be MFI P7242, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7242 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You received orders from General Mladic during Operation Zvijezda 94; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly from General Grubac. During Operation Zvijezda 94, my tactical group was resubordinated to the Herzegovina Corps which was in charge of all the activities to liberate the general area of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P731 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before us is an order you issued on 11 April 1994 related to Operation Zvijezda 94. I'd like to draw your attention to item 7 that states: "I am forwarding you a message from the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS, General Mladic, who visited our zone of combat operations on 10 April 1994." You then quote General Mladic's message as: "Keep pushing energetically onwards, pay no attention to what is going on around us. The Turks must disappear from these areas." This is the message you conveyed; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did General Mladic visit in your zone of operations on the 10th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at my observation post in the Sjenokos facility sector. It -- above the purpose reduction [as interpreted] facility Pobjeda. And it was during the night between the 10th and the 9th -- the 9th and the 10th, as far as I can remember. There was a group of fighters there. General Mladic addressed them as well. He told them to move forward and to liberate the area of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to be a little clear on where this observation post was, where was in relation to the town of Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to get my bearings as much as I can. In topographic terms, it was on the road leading from Gorazde to Mesici and Rogatica right before Jabucko Sedlo mountain pass, in the direction of Rogatica in that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So it was to the north of Gorazde, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how far from the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my estimate, some 7 to 8 kilometres. Maybe more, but everything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During Operation Zvijezda 94, the VRS committed crimes, including the shelling of civilian targets in Gorazde and summary executions of villagers who resided outside of the town of Gorazde. This is what happened; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The VRS again denied passage of convoys to Gorazde during this operation and also cut off the supply of electricity and water; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about electricity yesterday, but I don't know where the source is providing Gorazde and whether the army could have cut that off. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's just go to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 03464 for the witness. And, actually, if we could have page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is a 10 June 1994 United Nations report on the human rights situation in the former Yugoslavia. The report focuses on the situation in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the English original and page 4 of the B/C/S translation. Paragraph 5 of this report states: "The offensive with which this report is primarily concerned was first heralded by military actions in the last days of March 1994, including the blocking of the roads into the enclave, refusal to allow passage of convoys and the massing of troops at the edges of the safe area." This is what happened at the outset of the operation; right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The rest of paragraph 5 then discusses the penetration of the enclave by Bosnian Serb forces. Goes on to reference the 10 April air-strikes and eventually cease-fire on 23 April. This information is also correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 6, the report indicates that both sides continued to engage after the cease-fire. And then states: "Serious destruction has been caused during the withdrawal of attacking forces. They have also complicated the programme of medical evacuation from the enclave. According to international sources some 700 people were killed during the offensive and some 1.970 wounded. Deaths are continuing to occur due to sniping and other such incidents. During this and previous offensives, the town of Gorazde suffered damage to some 80 per cent of its buildings." The fact is the VRS killed or wounded a lot of people in the town of Gorazde during Operation Zvijezda 94. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have information about the number of casualties on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, paragraph 7, the report discusses the destruction of homes, individuals who attested to rapes, and summary executions of elderly women and a handicapped man, among other things. The paragraph then states: "At all stages of the offensive, villagers fled in fear of their lives, leaving behind homes, land and possessions." Again, this is what happened during the course of Operation Zvijezda 94 in the area of Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is on the basis of this document, but I claim that that's not the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Paragraphs 8, 9 and 10 discuss the deliberate targeting of civilian structures, specifically mentioning the hospital, along with how the Bosnian Serbs halted electricity and water supply which caused people --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to just stop for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, now it's the third time. Once more and you really -- I have to remove you from the courtroom. No speaking aloud. This is the last warning for today. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These paragraphs also describe how Bosnian Serbs halted the electricity and water supply which caused people to line up for water where they were then exposed to sniper fire. Just so you can see these paragraphs. Please let us know when you need the next page. I'm referring to paragraphs 8, 9, and 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And please give the witness time to read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could have the next page for the witness so he can continue reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you can please carry on reading on the next page, paragraph 10, and let us know when you are done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Turn the next page into -- in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, have you completed through paragraph 10?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The paragraphs you just read, they actually describe what happened during the operation; right? Civilian targets were deliberately targeted, there was no more water in the enclave and people were exposed to sniper fire when they went for water?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Units from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps were involved in the Operation Zvijezda 94; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside my area of responsibility, I don't know which units of theirs took part along that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I can then just focus you on paragraph 12, the report states: "It may be noted that the attack on the town of Gorazde involved the use of weapons of great destructive force." You requested modified air bombs which were used during this operation; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was at the very beginning of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this report into evidence, 65 ter 3464.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P7243, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 25361 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 3 April 1994 request from you to the VRS Main Staff and the Drina Corps. It refers to units attached to the SRK who have an air bomb launcher. This is -- the area that's being referred to, the axis, that's in your zone of responsibility; correct? Where it says "units attached to the SRK on the Mesici-Jabucko Sedlo axis"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this document you request ten FAB-100 kilogram air bombs and five fuel-charged ones. What was the calibre of the fuel-charged modified air bombs you were requesting? What was their payload?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: These bombs were never made in the first place. I just received information that was obviously incorrect. It was only classical air bombs that were made of 100, 150, and 275 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You used modified air bombs of these -- of the types you just mentioned during Operation Zvijezda 94; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just two projectiles, weight 100 kilograms, from the area of Jabucko Sedlo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 25361 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32232 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 20 April 1994 UNMO Gorazde shell rep update. It states: "Local sources report that moments ago two large-calibre 'ground to ground missiles' exploded near the city centre, destroying two houses and blowing the roofs off approximately 20 others." These two explosions were caused by the two modified air bombs you just told us you fired, right, this is what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. The range of those two bombs ensured activity up to the first facilities of the Pobjeda factory, not a metre further away from there. This is a totally false report of the local soldiers or civilians, I'm not going into that, who that was. We did not have that kind of range, as is referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the document into evidence, 65 ter 32232.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7245, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Witness, could you tell us, from where the bombs were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These bombs were fired from the area to the north of the pass of Jabucko Sedlo. That is to say, that faces Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the distance to the town centre of Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Jabucko Sedlo, the centre of town would be 10 or 12 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how were these projectiles propelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These projectiles were propelled with one rocket engine respectively, of a multiple rocket launcher of 122 millimetres called Grad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the range of such a propelling system, was that tested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was tested with one engine, with two engines, and with three engines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber received quite some evidence about modified air bombs, and one of the things that appeared several times is that the imprecision and the lack of exact knowledge of the effect of the propelling system. Do you have any comment on that or could you tell us how this exactly was tested, and when, and where, and how you received information about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, and I can speak with reliability. Air bombs were modified to such an extent that they were adjusted so as to have a rocket engine from the mentioned rocket-launcher placed on them. Also they had two sliding devices on their body, and they were supposed to guide the air bomb initially, and it's on part of a track, a rail track, or a tram track. It's that wide. And the point of these two parts was to give the initial direction to guide it in this way. It was tested in terms of targeting precision, and that was done by professional organs that is to say, engineers from the Pretis holding at the Kalinovik training grounds and with the assistance of certain professional institutions from Yugoslavia. On the basis of this testing, so as not to dwell on this for too long, firing tables were elaborated for all three types.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You had firing tables for the ones used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's right. Like for any other artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32311, e-court page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to be bringing up a previous portion of your Popovic testimony and I'll read it to you, starting at line 22. The question posed to you: "You mentioned air bombs. Were these weapons forbidden? Your answer was: "No." Next question: "But I thought we had heard here that these weapons were not particularly accurate. Could you tell us anything about this and about the accuracy of such weapons?" Your answer was: "It was precisely for those reasons that it was necessary to plan things in detail to avoid having casualties on your own side, because the launchers, launchers which - how shall I say this? - were fairly primitively manufactured, had not been tested technically. They hadn't been tested ballistically and so the way they were launched were not followed by necessary calculations, so these devices and this equipment was not precise. And very often there were very large deviations from one projectile to another." Sir, your statement to this Chamber, what you just explained about it being tested and them being accurate, it is not truthful. It is inconsistent with your previous testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous testimony, I spoke about the very beginning and about individual initiatives, so that individually and without centralised approval, such pieces be used. That is to say, unless all the measures that I mentioned during my previous testimony were not taken, that is to say, all these calculations, metallurgical, ballistic and all others, if that led to major mistakes and omissions. However, if all calculations were made and they had firing tables where all the parameters were for calculating repairs, then this lack of precision was drastically reduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is what you said during your previous testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said precisely for those cases where firing tables were not used and where all the corrections, improvements were not made.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I don't find as part of your previous testimony but let's read one other portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could I have e-court page 61. And we're going down to line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The question to you was: "These air bombs that you told us about, can you briefly describe how they actually were fired? I think you described a launching system and trailers and so forth, but can you just describe how they worked? " Your answer was: "In the briefest possible terms, you have a motor vehicle and the body of the vehicle in which you have incorporated part of a classical artillery piece known as the cradle. So all you have is the cradle without barrels, and welded on to that is a rail similar to a tram line or railway lines for trains. And this [sic] is the device used for launching. It has targeting devices from artillery pieces which was used for this cradle. "Now, the aerial bomb itself, as a whole, remains as it is. In order to launch it or to expel it from this device, at the back it had a metal adapter built into it, a metal plate or adapter, with an incised device for the rocket motor, 1, 2, 3, or 4 of those. And these rocket motors were used with multiple barrel rocket-launcher; specifically in this case, it was a multi-barrel of 122-millimetres of Russian manufacture called Grad, and on the underside there were two slips which led the bomb along the tracks or rails. And the third element was a device for electric activation, the activation of the motor itself and this activation was done on the side, on the flank, from a distance of about 10 metres. Since the rocket motors, once they are activated, expel the flare or flame, the substance of the -- that is how those aerial bombs were launched using this particular device." Do you stand by this testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There were no barrels like artillery to guide the launching of the modified rockets; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that you were promoted to the Main Staff after Operation Zvijezda 94?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a promotion. It is an official transfer to serve on the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this was a higher command than you had previously been serving; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of establishment, yes. But promotion is something completely different. I mean, if you take it literally, then promotion means promotion in rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we're approaching time for the break. I will finish during the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break first. Witness, you are invited to follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, when you referred to the modified air bombs in the previous testimony, could you please or either agree with the Defence or otherwise establish a time-frame, if there is any of such because the witness in his answer very much made a comment that may have been how it was in the beginning apart from, perhaps, that was not what you read to him but it would assist the Chamber if we could have more information about the time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It would be the Prosecution's position that the scope of his testimony related to 1995. And his time in the VRS Main Staff. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which would mean that what happened later on should have not been -- before 1995 but rather after 1995 or later in 1995. And Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's not the position of the Defence. It is inconsistent with the documents offered by the Prosecution into evidence and the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I said that it would assist the Chamber if it would have a time-frame. Apparently the parties disagree on the time-frame. If further attention could be paid to so that the Chamber receives assistance it considers relevant then that would be appreciated. We take a break, and resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the -- I wanted to say I would use the opportunity, but there are a few matters in relation to various witnesses which I would deal with perhaps not always completely in one breath. But it is about remaining issues from the testimony of Vojo Kupresanin and remaining issues from the testimony of Goran Krcmar, so if the parties would be on stand by for these two witnesses and any remaining issues I'll deal with them one by one, if there's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, meanwhile, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please, again, have 65 ter 32311, e-court page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I read you a portion of your Popovic testimony where you described the inaccuracy of modified air bombs. I just want to return to that page and direct your attention to something earlier on that same page just for some context. Starting at line 4, you were asked the question and this is while you were being shown an order: "Do you remember where you were when you drafted this order? Were you still serving in Crna Rijeka or were you already in Zvornik? Your answer was: "In Crna Rijeka." Do you stand by this testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: What order are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay, let's go onto the order that you were being shown at that time. It is actually one of the associated exhibits to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have D956, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where do we find that. In relation to what paragraph of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But I'm checking just to verify. Yes, paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, before you was the order that you were commenting upon during your Popovic testimony. It is a Main Staff urgent order for artillery and rocket support to units in Operation Spreca 95, dated 30 March 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see that even in this order you are directly referred to a part of a team of the VRS Main Staff in your position as chief of artillery, in the context of planning tactical and technical preparation and use of the aforementioned equipment.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The answers that you were providing in the Popovic case were clearly in the context of your position in the Main Staff in 1995. That was the case; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution notes that it's marked for identification. We have no objection so I can leave it for the housekeeping but we would ask to have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's one of the ones that's tentatively assigned a number by Mr. Registrar so it's not yet been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there's no need to assign a further number to it. We -- if there would be any reason that the Chamber would consider to deny admission then, of course, we would, of course, you because then you tender it as well. Nothing of the kind at this moment is to be expected. One additional -- oh, perhaps I should address the parties. In view of the time-frame and in view of the answers given by the witnesses, if any party would have access to any of the firing tables the witness referred to, the Chamber would, of course, appreciate to be informed about it, and perhaps to be provided with it. Witness, do you have any knowledge about where these firing tables were to be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I had them while I was an active-duty officer. I had them in my hands. Where you could find them now, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you have any explanation as where you said, My answer that I gave at the time were at the very early stages, the beginning of the use of aerial bombs, where they were not tested yet. But when you used them they were tested. The context given now is Operation Spreca which was in 1995, so therefore perhaps would you have an explanation why you considered for Operation Spreca, them still not being tested, or at least in that context you gave that evidence that they were not tested. Yet you told us today in 1994 they had been tested and that you had firing tables. Do you have any explanation as far as the chronology you relied on is concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I can remember, I got questions about aerial bombs whereas in Spreca operation, launchers, crews and a team that carried out technical preparation did all that based on all the existing documents and the existing firing tables. So the period in question was not the first time aerial bombs were used. I was there myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not exactly an answer to my question, but let's move on. Please proceed. And why is it not an answer to my question? Because the answers you gave earlier about aerial bombs not being tested were apparently put to you in a time-frame which dealt with Operation Spreca which is, I think, mentioned even in that context in the -- in the -- in the testimony. I leave it to that, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the document that is at issue is on the screen still, and if you read it I think you will see that it talks about checking the readiness of crews so would have referred to things that have not been done before, that are now being checked to see if they've been implemented. So, I think Your Honours are actually --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'd just ask that we be careful in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm trying to be very careful. That's why I'm directing Your Honours to look at the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that what's I did. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32229 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, I just have a couple more documents to go through with you. This is a Drina Corps Command request dated 8 April 1995 related to Spreca 95. It's to the VRS Main Staff. It says: "In order to swiftly break the enemy's resistance in Spreca 95 operation, the chief of ARJ, Colonel Masal, suggested the use of three FAB-250 and one-time asb, 275 kilogram on 9 April 1995. Please consider the Colonel's suggestion and approve the uses of the suggested quantities." Sent from General Zivanovic. This is what you requested for the operation; correct? You were personally requesting the use of aerial bombs.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Zivanovic requested and I agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at the next page in both versions. Before us, we have the response from General Milovanovic dated the same day, 8 April 1995, sent back to the Drina Corps and it says: "In response to your request ... the Main Staff hereby approves the use of the mentioned ordnance. The use of the ordnance is to be controlled solely by Colonel Dragisa Masal." This is what happened during Operation Spreca 95; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that you're evading or trying to recouch your testimony from the Popovic case because you yourself controlled the use of the modified air bombs as a member of the Main Staff. That's what you're doing today.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. Be precise. I personally controlled and managed the preparations of this ordnance for Operation Spreca 95. How would it look if a colonel participated in the preparation of ordnance for each activity? He would then be a lieutenant or a commander of a squad. Of course, I was in charge of the technical preparation of those things, of that ordnance; that's only understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7246, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 15428.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a Main Staff report to the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic, dated 15 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have page 3, I believe in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to focus your attention on the section related to the zone of the IBK, the Eastern Bosnia Corps and the situation in the corps. The report says: "Corps units responded to all of the enemy attacks. On Majevica, the main efforts are focussed on fortification of current positions, reconnaissance and preparation of units for reclaiming of lost positions; one FAB-250 and one napalm bomb were fired at Krstac village ..." And we see there's some handwriting which has been translated: "As retaliation for fire opened on the general area of Bijeljina, while 17 122-millimetre shells and one FAB-250 kilogram were fired at Urajevo village as retaliation for frequent shelling of Brcko." Sir the fact is you were firing modified air bombs as retaliation for other actions; right? You were doing that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... this is about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has given an opportunity to explain what seems to be contradicting evidence. Please explain, Witness, what you'd like to say about the firing of projectiles in retaliation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is about the redeployment of the Eastern Bosnia Corps. This activity has nothing to do with the chief of artillery of the Main Staff. Personally at the time, I was in the western part of Bosnia in the Drvar sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next question arises whether you deny that it happened or that you are just telling that you were not involved. Which of the two is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if that happened, but clearly this is a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Weber, but perhaps you should be very precise. If you said this is what you did, that you clarify what you mean by "you," whether that was the Bosnian Serb army or whether it was this witness. So please be very precise in your questions. Then I think we have not yet decided on the admission. Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7247.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7247 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you took up your position as chief of artillery in the Main Staff, you visited all the corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not the Herzegovina Corps. I only visited that corps after six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32227 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 24 September 1994 VRS Main Staff order from General Milovanovic. In item 1, there's a reference to the Chief of Staff of the artillery organ of the Main Staff carrying out an inspection. This is a reference to the inspections that you carried out of the corps at the time, when you became the chief of artillery; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 2, there's a schedule for the inspection of the VRS corps and other units. With -- noting what you said about the Herzegovina Corps, you followed the -- you inspected the artillery and rocket units of the other corps and units according to the schedule; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise, I did not inspect all artillery and rocket units. I inspected their commands, and I was briefed by the chiefs of artillery of those commands. I inspected only those artillery units that I deemed to be important and that I thought I should inspect. Those were usually artillery regiments as the highest-ranking artillery units in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go to item 4, and this is on the next page in the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Irrespective of what the "inspection" exactly meant, could you confirm that did you that inspection in accordance with the schedule, because that was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not in accordance with the schedule because I did not visit the Herzegovina Corps. I was sent on a different mission which was a priority at the time, which was more important than this inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember, then, what you did in the evening hours of the 25th of October, up to the -- 2.00 on the 26th of October? What was it that did you then, in 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, certain positions in the zone of the 2nd Krajina Corps were lost and the IKM of the Main Staff was set up in the zone of the 2nd Corps. So together with General Milovanovic, I went on that mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to item 4. They're specifications on what the corps commands or the commands were to report on. One of the items relates to the "grouping of the artillery formation of" - and it's in the document as KOGs and Br AGs - "possibility of regrouping by calibre while adhering to the usage principles." Is it correct that this is a typo in this sentence and it should be referring to KAGs or corps artillery groups, not KOG.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that here but I know what you are talking about. We are talking about KAGs, and that stands for corps artillery groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... you should give an opportunity to the witness to look at the next page. Please enlarge the upper part. Third line, KOG is an error, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not KOG. It should be KAG. This is the abbreviation for the corps artillery group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you received reports back from the different corps you inspected related to the matters in item 4; right? And please let us know if you need to go either forward or backward in the document -- well, actually there is no forward, so let us know if you need to see the first page again.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there's no need. I received reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On these items. During your inspections you received reports on these items that we see in the order under number 4; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 32227 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7248, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. Mr. Ivetic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us a time indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: About one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that we can't conclude the testimony of the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, again, General?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, at transcript page 33356, lines 9 through 25, you were talking about an UNPROFOR convoy that was delayed the longest at the Rogatica check-point and it was not clear to what time-period this delay entailed. Could you please tell us in terms of the number of days how long was the longest delay of a convoy that was stopped at check-points in your zone of responsibility, while at the Tactical Group Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to make things abundantly clear, this convoy that was delayed for three days, what was the reason for the delay of that convoy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only reason was the fact that the convoy leaders did not accept or rather did not allow inspection as agreed by the agreement on the freedom of movement of convoys through Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, to make abundantly clear what we're talking of, was this convoy eventually inspected?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eventually at the end of day three, the UNPROFOR command intervened. Their representatives arrived from Sarajevo and they allowed inspection, but one vehicle belonging to the observers was removed from the convoy and went back to Sarajevo voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the vehicles that were searched, was anything out of the ordinary discovered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Video cameras were discovered. Some optical surveillance tools, binoculars, radio sets, and as far as I can remember, there were also some clips for automatic weapons, as well as satellite telephones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving along, in relation to the ban on movement of convoys, you also said yesterday at transcript page 33354 that this was when relationships with UNPROFOR were tense. Could you please explain for us what it is you meant when you said, "Relationships with UNPROFOR were tense"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, and at that level, at which -- Can you hear what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time while I was in that position, we received information from the superior command, and it was stated why certain convoys were disallowed. Usually the accompanying documents said due to misunderstandings or some deterioration in relations between the UNPROFOR Command in Sarajevo and the Serb side. That is why convoys were not allowed to enter territory that was under control of units of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And yesterday, sir, there was talk of the time-period of May 1993. Do you recall what the particular tension or deterioration in relations between UNPROFOR and the Serb side was in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, at the time, at the time there was a danger or, rather, a threat to the following: That the positions of Republika Srpska would be bombed by NATO air force ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to turn to your statement, D942 marked for identification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you going to a new subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Same subject [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no, no, then I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it's D942 marked for identification, page 11 English and it's between pages 9 and 10 in the Serbian, and it's paragraph 23 which deals with the same topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in regard to these times that the relations were tense with UNPROFOR, you identify a document from April of 1994 in paragraph 23 of your statement, and you state that the Supreme Commander kept in force the ban on the movement of teams and convoys of UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations. Now I'd like to look at P00780, which is the document that you cite here, and I'd like to turn to the last page and last paragraph of that document. And, sir, I'd like to explain your conclusion which we just saw in paragraph 23 of your statement in relation to this paragraph of this document that you have cited to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know how your question was translated -- interpreted, Mr. Ivetic, you said I'd like to explain. But did you invite the witness to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise I meant to say I'd like the witness to explain why that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the witness may not understand that he's asked to do something. Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, precisely in this order, it is stated that on the basis of the decision of the Supreme Command to suspend all contacts or all relations between the VRS Main Staff and the command of the United Nations force. On the basis of that decision of the Supreme Command, an order was issued to the Main Staff, and the Main Staff conveyed that order to all of their subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm moving to a related but slightly different topic so if Your Honours had something to ask I would defer to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there was one matter. Yesterday there was the issue of the longest delay and that was about three weeks which was put to you by the Prosecution. You remember? The convoy was kept at a check-point for three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My recollection, just to be fair to the witness, was actually at the time what I put was that there were no convoys allowed into the area for three weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may have misunderstood that. I'm happy I raised the issue because it improves my understanding of the testimony but the question is not needed any further. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the convoys, yesterday you were asked about alleged food shortages in Gorazde and that was several times but I am focussing particularly on the instance at transcript page 33365 and at that instance, the source that was presented to you was a news article by Agence France Presse. What was your experience during the war as to the accuracy of news journalists reporting as to the situation in and around Gorazde town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall respond as a soldier. If one were to believe all the information from the media, electronic and written, then during one month of war everybody would have died of thirst and hunger in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So propaganda in view of the safe areas, especially the safe area of Gorazde, was catastrophic, and it just prolonged the war in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you were also asked about food -- about the lack of convoys going to Zepa causing food problems and that's at transcript page 33357 through 33358. I'd like to call up number 25880 and page 1 in both the English and the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Ivetic, since we'll not be able to conclude the testimony of the witness anyhow if we start with a new document now and then a series of questions ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see your point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore I would suggest that we look at that next week. Witness, I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. We'd like to see you back Monday, 9.30 in the morning. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume Monday, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar reminds me of something but there's some misunderstanding perhaps. The response by the Prosecution on any scheduling issue and time or from preparation, I understood that it would be filed today, but if that is a wrong understanding, then I'd like to hear from the Prosecution now what their response is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I presume this in connection with the proposed adjournment issue? Yes, we are working on that and expect to file it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: File it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I understood it to be. But apparently some others thought that we would receive an oral response today. We will wait and see -- the Chamber may even, once we have seen that and if we had made up our mind as far as scheduling is concerned, the Chamber may consider to already inform the parties informally on what it has decided or what it intends to decide so as to -- if there are any compelling reasons -- not in terms of whether you want more or less time, but compelling reasons that what we have on our mind in terms of what weeks or what month, et cetera, that if that would find strong opposition, really compelling opposition, that we will consider whether we will send already such a message before, or whether we already will inform you about the final outcome of our deliberations on how to proceed. And this -- I know that everyone is waiting for it because it may affect your personal programmes as well, so we will deliver that as soon as we can. We adjourn for the day, and we resume on Monday, the 23rd of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 23rd day of March, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
